subject: general
question: A boat travels 14 km upstream in 14 hours and 171 km downstream in 9 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Upstream Speed** (u) = 14 ÷ 14 = 1 km/hr

**Downstream Speed** (v) = 171 ÷ 9 = 19 km/hr

**Still Water Speed** = (u + v) ÷ 2 = (1 + 19) ÷ 2 = 10 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 10 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Upstream distance = 14 km, Upstream time = 14 hours

Downstream distance = 171 km, Downstream time = 9 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed in Still Water (x) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a173b0dffb1723dcd4dd1d053e8f91771e9fffb269d9c39ed9279105b597b4bf.png] 
**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream Speed (u) = 14 km ÷ 14 hr = 1 km/hr

⇒ Downstream Speed (v) = 171 km ÷ 9 hr = 19 km/hr

⇒ Speed of boat in still water (x) = (19 + 1) ÷ 2

⇒ x = 20 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 10 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 10 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Stream

The speed of the current or stream (y) is calculated as half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: y = (v − u) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed in Water

Downstream speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream (x + y); Upstream speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream (x − y).

Average Speed of Boat

If a boat travels a certain distance and returns to the starting point, Average Speed = (u × v) ÷ x, where x is speed in still water.</p
